key_insight: A very small, interpretable two-parameter model (DynaBase) can match strong zero-shot dynamical-system reconstruction performance by blending the current latent state with the nearest in-context neighbor and its successor.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests that high-performing foundation-model behavior for dynamical systems may be achievable with far fewer parameters, making reconstruction models simpler, cheaper, and easier to optimize directly.
method: Iteratively reduce the prior SOTA DynaMix model to a minimal interpretable form.
Use a linear blend of the current latent state and nearest in-context neighbor plus temporal successor to generate forecasts.
Analyze a 1-parameter family of maps that spans context-parroting to bounded chaotic behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports highly competitive zero-shot reconstruction across chaotic and cyclic systems, with many orders of magnitude fewer parameters than other foundation models.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated from the abstract-level summary, so the generality of the minimal form may still depend on the chosen training strategy and reconstruction setting.
paper_title: A Minimal Interpretable Architecture for Zero-Shot Reconstruction of Dynamical Systems
